title: Cups in the Half-Light
prompt: The first glimmer of dawn shows in the windows. The Open Floor is dark and quiet. Nora has arrived early and is setting out cups at each desk for the day ahead. She pauses at the Party Member's corner desk, then leaves a cup there too, though it will remain untouched. Why does she persist in this small ritual?

title: Reason Codes
prompt: Early in the Moonwell room, Theo, Maren and Julian lean over Maren's laptop, debating the wording of a shared document. Theo thinks the reason codes are clear; Maren has numbered the points for translation; Julian is trying out taglines that focus on the customer. The document needs to go to Owen soon but they're not ready to send it. Is it enough to show the codes, or should they explain them too?

title: Plain Terms
prompt: Late afternoon in the Glass Box. Graham has brought Maren a paragraph of dense, jargony client-speak and is leaning back in the CEO's chair, asking for a translation into plain terms. Maren has the original text on a screen and is methodically restating it in her own numbered points, each one starting with a clear 'For whom...' as she goes. Graham nods at each point but holds up a finger at the last one. Is it really that simple, or has something been lost in translation?

title: Third Strike
prompt: Late afternoon on the Open Floor. Owen sits with the spare laptop, watches one test fail for the third time, and writes a precise note about it. Anselm is within earshot at a nearby desk or doorway and could be drawn in. Is this failure significant enough to warrant attention, or just an outlier that can be ignored?

title: History and Hacks
prompt: Early in the day on the Open Floor. Theo, the Engineer, is asking Brody, the Tech Lead, about an old function in the codebase. Brody, known for his slow, thoughtful manner and deep knowledge, responds with 'Hm' and proceeds to share the history behind the function's existence, delving into the reasons it was implemented and the challenges it was meant to address. Theo listens, intrigued, as Brody's explanation reveals the hacks and workarounds that have shaped the code over time. Will Brody's historical perspective help Theo understand the function better?

title: Late-Night Analogies
prompt: Late at night in the darkened office, Theo is the only one still working. He paces between the desks, trying out different explanations for how Fraud-Stop works: a nightclub bouncer, a river ferry, an elevator in a tall building. He speaks each one aloud to the empty room, listening to how they sound. Is there one that will finally make sense to the others, or is it still just a tangle of code and metaphors?

title: Last Run
prompt: Evening on the Open Floor. Brody is waiting at Owen's desk for the last full test run to finish before he will approve a merge. Owen is watching the progress bar and tapping his fingers on the desk, one finger for each percent. The run is taking longer than usual and the room feels slow and heavy. Brody finally breaks the silence with a quiet question about the cause of the delay. Owen gives a number but it doesn't explain much. What is taking the tests so long?

title: Staging Fears
prompt: Late morning. Theo, laptop under one arm, crouches in the Server Closet, fingers busy on the staging rack. Owen watches from the doorway, arms crossed. The hum is loud, the green light is steady. 'Tell me this won't break live,' says Theo, only half-joking. 'I'll tell you when it breaks test,' Owen replies. Is the silence of the server a good sign or a bad one?

title: Latency and a Question
prompt: The Open Floor, a few minutes after the 06:00 standup. Brody has tapped the latency graph twice and settled into his chair, looking at his screens. Theo sits across from him, wanting to ask about yesterday's spike in the graph. He's already said 'So, about that latency--' but Brody didn't look up. Theo is trying to decide whether to wait for eye contact, or just ask. How bad was the spike, and will it happen again?

title: Opening Gambit
prompt: In the Glass Box at lunchtime, Graham and Julian are practicing a call opening. Graham speaks, then asks 'Fair?' each time. Julian nods, then gives him a new opening to try. They've done it three times so far. The prospect is a bank. On the desk, Julian's neat stack of index cards has one card face up with 'Reliability' underlined twice. Will they find a way to say 'reliable' that feels fresh?

title: Double Shot Deadline
prompt: Evening in the Kitchen. The clock above the Glass Box shows 20:10. Owen is hunched at the old table, fingers laced around a fresh double shot of espresso, steeling himself for the last test run. Nora bustles in with a bright, 'Love, you've got to keep your strength up!' and slides the little cup towards him. She lingers, her eyes flicking between the clock and his pale face. Will the late run pass in time for the release notes, or will she have to bring him a triple next time?

title: Late Shift
prompt: Late evening on the Open Floor. Nora is tidying up the kitchen and wiping down the table while Brody watches the latency graph, tapping it twice before looking up. They are the last two left in the office for the night. Nora hums a tune as she works, glancing at the clock. Brody's eyes keep returning to the graph, his face unreadable. Will they make small talk, or just continue in their separate worlds until one of them leaves for the night?

title: Plans and Printouts
prompt: Late evening in the Moonwell room. Maren is finishing up a plan note in green ink, tidying the printouts into neat piles. Graham stands in the doorway, within earshot. He watches her work, a folded index card in his hand. Maren glances up, catches his eye. 'Another plan for our friends in Sales?' he asks, trying for lightness. Maren straightens, taps her pen on the papers. 'For whom?' she asks, not quite smiling. Does he want a logistics metaphor, or just an answer?

title: Numbers and Espresso
prompt: The sun is rising outside the kitchen window. Owen sits at the old table, waiting for his espresso to cool, and for the numbers on the folded paper to make sense. Nora bustles in, sees him, and puts the small cup down with a clink. 'Love,' she says, patting his shoulder, then she's gone. He thanks her by counting the results out loud, but the last number is lower than he expected. Why is the trend down?

title: The Client's Voice
prompt: Morning in the Moonwell room. Julian has a tagline that needs the weight of a client's words behind it. Maren has the numbers and the client stories, but she wants to know which one he's thinking of using and what he's really saying about Fraud-Stop with it. Julian leans back in his chair, confident; Maren leans forward, pen uncapped. Whose promise will it be in the end - the client's, Julian's, or Fraud-Stop's?

title: Stable but Wobbly
prompt: Late afternoon in the Glass Box. Graham, Julian, and Maren huddle by Julian's whiteboard, which shows three client logos. Graham points at Ostry and speaks in the metaphor of a wobbly wheel on a well-loaded cart. Maren raises an eyebrow and writes 'for whom?' on her pad. Julian looks at his watch and says 'stable' like he's announcing a plane's altitude. Is Ostry stable, or just not yet tipping over?

title: Analogies at the Harbour
prompt: Mid-morning at the edge of the Open Floor. Theo is talking to himself, trying to explain a COUNTRYMISMATCH error using a ferry analogy, but gets stuck at the harbour. Julian, overhearing from a nearby desk, wonders if the explanation could be tweaked to resonate with their target customers. The question hangs in the air: is the ferry analogy helpful or just confusing the issue?

title: Overheard Planning
prompt: Late morning on the Open Floor. Maren is at her desk, quietly reading through a numbered plan she's about to hand over, making small changes as she goes. At a nearby desk, Graham is within earshot and can't help but overhear snippets. She starts to explain to herself why point three is now point two, but stops, realizing she's not alone. Will Graham ask what she's working on, or will Maren wait for a more formal handover?

title: Code and Coffee
prompt: Late afternoon on the Open Floor. Brody is reading Theo's latest code changes on his left screen, his eyes occasionally flicking to the latency graph on his right. Theo has just brought back two espressos from the Kitchen and is waiting for feedback, trying not to fiddle with the cups. The question is: are these changes ready to ship, or does Theo need to go around again? The tech lead's silence is making the engineer nervous.

title: Night Watch
prompt: Just before 05:00, Nora stands in the darkened reception, checking the key ring against her list. The last light from the Open Floor reflects off the polished floor. She looks up and down the rows of desks and chairs, tidied and waiting for the day. Her hand is on the final switch; the door is ready to lock behind her. The night has been quiet and she's glad of that. Is the calm of an empty office a small victory, or just how it should be?

title: The Long Beat
prompt: Owen is at his desk on the Open Floor, running the full test suite. Theo is at the nearby coffee station, chatting idly while filling a mug. The tests run and Owen stares at the results for a long, silent moment before noting a single number on a card. Theo, sensing the tension, falls quiet. Will Owen share the number or keep it to himself? And what does that number really mean for the project?

title: End of the Line
prompt: Late evening on the Open Floor. Graham stops by, asking about the state of the deployment pipeline. Theo makes a crack about ships and trains, but Owen gives a crisp status report, ending with the number of tests still outstanding. Graham nods, but is clearly weighing whether to press for details. Theo senses the moment stretching and starts to riff on cargo and containers, but Owen cuts in with another number. Is the shipment ready to sail, or does it need more time at the dock?

title: Night Questions
prompt: The kitchen is dark and silent, lit only by the green glow of the emergency exit sign. Julian sits at the table, practicing a question under his breath, ready to catch Brody first thing in the morning. The weight of the closed office presses in from all sides. What secret doubt could drive a marketer to rehearse his pitch in an empty room?

title: One Last Check
prompt: Late evening on the Open Floor. Brody, coat half on, is tapping the latency graph for the second time. Theo, loitering by the door with his own coat over his arm, thinks it's a ritual for good luck, but it's really a test of Brody's own patience. The last test run is ticking down; the graph should be steady; the release notes should be done. Brody glances from graph to clock to coat, then back again. Is there time for one more check before the end of the Ship watch?

title: For Whom?
prompt: Early morning on the Open Floor. Maren is poised over a fresh sheet of paper, red ink drying on her opening question. She taps the pen, considering her next point. Julian is nearby, straightening brochures with an eye on his watch. The room is quiet but for the hum of servers and the distant clink of Nora putting the kitchen in order. Maren's mind is on the work ahead; Julian's thoughts are already out the door and onto the street. Will today's plans start with the user or the market?

title: Velocity in a Nutshell
prompt: Early on the Open Floor, Theo is explaining the velocity rule to Julian over the snack shelf, using a new analogy about cars and traffic. Julian is nodding slowly, one hand on the coffee pot, trying to picture how it fits with what he's heard from clients. Theo has not yet mentioned time zones or averages. Is there an analogy that will finally click for Julian, or a question that will turn the lightbulb on for Theo?

title: Overnight Numbers
prompt: Early morning on the Open Floor. Owen has just finished reporting the overnight test suite results to Brody, stating two numbers without any commentary. Brody taps the latency graph twice before leaning back in his chair, absorbing the information. Owen has more to say but is waiting for a signal. Brody knows there's a story behind those numbers but doesn't want to ask directly. Will Owen volunteer the details or will Brody have to prompt him?

title: The Last Number
prompt: Late evening on the Open Floor. Owen reads out the last result of the day in a flat, deadpan voice, then writes it down. A single number. Brody is within earshot at a nearby desk, putting away his keyboard for the night. The number seems to hang in the air between them. Owen's pen hovers over the notebook. Does the number mean what Owen thinks it means? What would Brody think?

title: Evening Crisps Debate
prompt: Late evening in the Kitchen. Theo and Julian have stayed late to grab supper from the snack shelf and debate a question they plan to bring up at tomorrow's lunch. Theo is chatting rapidly, punctuating his points with crisp crunches. Julian is calmly sipping his drink and trying out different phrasings of a counterargument. The question is still forming, and they're both aware that it could change the room's opinion if phrased right. How can they make their case without tipping the balance?

title: Quiet Reflections
prompt: Late at night on the dark Open Floor, Theo Palliser sorts through his sticky notes, stacking the ones marked 'easy' that he's crossed out. The office is quiet and still, with only the hum of the servers breaking the silence. As he tidies up, Theo reflects on the day's challenges and whether his usual jokes and bravado are enough to cover his doubts. In the solitude of the night, what is he really thinking about his work and his place at Ashiorid?

title: Early Values
prompt: Pre-dawn in the Kitchen. Only the under-cabinet lights are on. Nora has come in early to sort the supplies and is boiling a kettle for tea. She reads the values card by the door, tracing the words with a finger. 'Love and pet.' She smiles, remembers a joke about what the values would be if they were honest. The kitchen timer ticks down. What's the most honest value?

title: Overnight Results
prompt: In the Small Room, the fluorescent light buzzes and flickers. Theo has pulled an all-nighter and looks it; Owen is crisp, his shirt still sharp at 5:40am. Owen reads the printout of overnight test results, his finger moving down the page. Theo slumps, eyes red, and tries a weak joke about being up all night with a sick test. Owen gives a number back, no expression. Did the tests pass, or is there still work to do before the day shift arrives?

title: The Watchful Night
prompt: Deep in the night, the Open Floor is dark and still. Only the glow of monitors and the hum of servers break the silence. Owen sits alone at a spare laptop, his eyes fixed on the progress of the overnight test suite. With each passing minute, he counts the growing tally of successful tests under his breath. The room feels empty, yet the weight of the company's future hangs heavy in the air. Will the tests continue their steady march, or will an unexpected failure cast a shadow over the coming day?

title: Nightly Rounds
prompt: Deep in the night, the office is dark and quiet. At her station, Nora methodically goes through her closing-up checklist, marking each item with a soft pencil tick. She opens the breaker box and counts the switches, then moves to the first-aid kit, checking the supplies are complete. Her keychain jingles softly as she works. The tasks are routine, but she performs them with care. Is there anything in the dark office that needs her attention tonight?

title: Watching the Graph
prompt: It's just past 05:00 and Brody is the only one at Ashiorid. He sits at his desk in the dark, facing the window, the glow of the latency graph casting a faint light on his face. The graph pulses with each passing second, the lines dipping and rising like the breaths of Fraud-Stop itself. Brody watches the graph intently, lost in thought, as the city outside begins to stir. What secrets does the graph hold that keeps him here so late?

title: The Easy That Wasn't
prompt: Early on the Open Floor, Theo's stuck on an estimate. He's scribbled 'easy' on a sticky note, crossed it out, and is now circling a much bigger number. Julian's nearby, either at his desk or in the doorway, and can't help but overhear the muttered math. Theo's trying to joke his way out of a gaffe; Julian's trying to decide whether to ask, or to wait and see. Will Theo's second guess be any more solid than his first?

title: Joke and a Number
prompt: Late afternoon on the Open Floor. Theo has just finished a feature and sent Owen a test request, trying to lighten the moment with a joke. Owen replies with a count of how many tests will be run, his tone flat and deadpan. Theo chuckles, but looks a little cornered as he spins back to his screen. Owen is already in the testing dashboard, the numbers starting to roll in. Is the joke more important than the number, or is it the other way around?

title: Line by Line
prompt: Early on the Open Floor. Maren has pulled Theo aside to ask about a single line of code from last week's big change. He's explaining it as a series of 'and then's, waving his hands. She's taking structured notes, circling 'For whom?' in red. The change is already live but she wants to know what she missed. Is there a reason for this line, or did it just get caught up in the rush?

title: Feedback with Footnotes
prompt: Near the end of the Ship watch, Maren is in the Moonwell room with Julian's draft one-pager, marking it up with her red pencil. He's pitched his tagline aloud three times, but she's focused on her footnotes and keeps tapping the page with 'For whom?' circled. Julian wants her to get to the good parts; Maren wants him to see the gaps. The paper shuffles between them. Is the message the medium, or the other way around?

title: Quiet Night, Full In-tray
prompt: Late night at the darkened reception desk. Nora has let herself in with a torch and is quietly sorting through the post tray, aligning the edges of the envelopes with the edge of the desk. She's a silhouette against the street lights through the frosted glass doors. Soon she'll leave everything tidy for the morning and lock up behind her. Will she notice the odd white envelope with no stamp, just a name?

title: Seen Through?
prompt: Late evening in the Kitchen. Nora has the last pastry on a plate, offering it to Graham with a bright smile. Graham thanks her warmly, but with a clipped edge, like a man who suspects his late-night habits have not gone unnoticed. He takes the plate, raising it in a small salute. Nora busies herself with wiping the table, but her eyes keep flicking back to him. Does she know more than she lets on, or is Graham just feeling the long day?

title: End of Day Rounds
prompt: The small hours in the dimly lit Kitchen. Nora methodically sorts through the day's bin streams, making sure each is in its proper place for morning pickup. She runs a hand along the snack shelf, noting what needs restocking. Her key ring jingles softly as she double-checks each door is securely locked. Satisfied, she pauses for a moment, surveying her tidy domain. Is there anything else to be done before she can finally head home?

title: Late Night, Empty Office
prompt: Late at night on the Open Floor, only two desk lamps break the darkness. Maren is deep into a numbered list, writing and crossing out in red ink. Brody is motionless in his chair, facing his dark screens. They have not spoken for hours. The silence feels charged; each hears the other breathe. Maren stretches, and her chair creaks. Brody taps the desk, twice. What would it take for either to say goodnight and leave the other alone with their thoughts?

title: Urgent Ticket
prompt: Morning on the Open Floor. Theo, the Engineer, reads out a new ticket from Ostry Mercantile with an alarming subject line. Owen, the Tester, sits up and asks for the ticket number, ignoring Theo's commentary. The ticket is only minutes old and the urgency is clear. How bad is it, really? And who else will be reading that subject line today?

title: Pipeline Promises
prompt: Eleven in the morning in the bright Kitchen. Julian is just back from the Moonwell room and is humming the jingle as he picks at the last Danish on the snack shelf. Nora has followed him in with the whiteboard and is asking, nicely but firmly, that he keep his pipeline chart off the Kitchen wall from now on. Julian's charm is set to 'apology' and his hands are up in surrender. Will his promise last until lunch?

title: Morning Snack Stock
prompt: Early in the Kitchen. Theo is hovering, hand out for the last of the granola bars. Nora has the box open and is restocking the snack shelf, making it neat, like she makes everything neat. 'Pet,' she says, but does not quite smile. Theo takes his time unsleeving the two biscuits he picked out first. Is this how it's going to be all week, the two of them circling the shelf?

title: Pitch and Parry
prompt: Late afternoon in the Glass Box. Julian, in a careful tone, is pitching a new slogan for the upcoming product release to Graham across the desk. Graham leans back, listening, and then asks whether the tagline will resonate with their biggest client, Malmont Savings & Trust. Julian's smile doesn't waver, but his eyes flicker to the window. Does the right line depend on the audience?

title: Five Runs, Five Numbers
prompt: Early afternoon on the Open Floor. Owen is rerunning a test for the fifth time, each number joining the column on his card. Brody watches from the Server Closet doorway, a slight frown on his face. The test is taking longer than usual and the results are all over the place. Owen taps the card with his pen, considering. Will a consistent result emerge, or is there a deeper problem? Brody clears his throat, but doesn't step forward.

title: Late Verdict
prompt: Late evening on the Open Floor. Theo is watching Brody's face for any flicker of approval or objection as the last small merge of the day goes through. Brody is expressionless, his eyes flicking from the latency graph to the merge request and back again. The evening test run is starting and neither has moved for a coffee. Is the code ready to ship or will they find something to talk about until midnight?

title: Night Shift Chat
prompt: The darkened Open Floor, after midnight. The Party Member sits silently at the corner desk, unmoving, as Nora bustles in from the kitchen. She sets a fresh cup of tea beside the closed notebook and aligns the pen just so. 'You're burning the midnight oil again, I see,' she says cheerfully to the empty room, hands on hips. 'I don't mind a late one myself now and then, but you know what they say about all work and no play.' She smiles, but there's no one there to see it. Will the Party Member break their silence tonight?

title: Numbers and Timelines
prompt: Late morning in the Open Floor. Maren has fixed the tab colours on a printout and starts her first numbered list of the day, glancing at the clock above the Glass Box between points. Julian is within earshot at a nearby desk, leaning back in his chair and absently spinning a pen between his fingers. He's trying out a new tagline under his breath, but Maren's structured points are drawing his attention. Will he be pulled into the discussion, or will he stay focused on his own task?

title: Overnight Run Results
prompt: Early morning on the Open Floor. Owen is at his desk with the overnight run printed out, carefully noting totals in his notebook. Fourteen of fifteen passed again. Theo is nearby, pretending not to listen but clearly curious. Owen keeps his pen moving and his eyes down. Will Theo bite and ask about the one that failed, or will Owen be left alone with his numbers and his usual laconic report at the next standup?

title: Promise and Pizzazz
prompt: Afternoon in the Moonwell room. Maren has a numbered list of what Fraud-Stop can and can't reliably do. Julian is trying out bold, simple taglines that promise more. They're both aware that customers want something between the two. Maren keeps asking 'For whom?'; Julian keeps flipping his pen. Is it possible to be honest and exciting at the same time?

title: Waiting for the Screen
prompt: The Moonwell room, mid-morning. Maren is pinning a printed diagram to the cork wall, blocking and unblocking the slow screen with her body as she works. Julian stands by, pad in hand, waiting for the screen to wake so he can bring up the customer journey map. They're both thinking about the meeting with Halvard & Sons later. Maren has already written 'For whom?' at the top of her list. Is the screen going to be ready before they need to start?

title: Afternoon Strategy
prompt: Late afternoon in the Moonwell room. Graham, Maren, and Brody have the cork wall to themselves. Graham, standing by the slow screen, wants a one-sentence plan from Maren and Brody for the rest of the day. Maren has a list of steps, Brody has numbers in mind. Maren taps her pen against her teeth; Brody watches the screen. They both know the afternoon could go a dozen ways. What does Graham want to hear?

title: End of Day Routines
prompt: Late evening in the Kitchen. Nora is tidying up, taking out the bins and wiping down the table with brisk efficiency. She turns off the temperamental espresso machine with a firm click. Brody, nearby in the doorway to the Server Closet, watches her go through her end-of-day rituals. The hum of the servers fills the silence between them. Will Brody stay to finish his work, or call it a day and join Nora in her wind-down routine?

title: Afternoon Margins
prompt: Late afternoon on the Open Floor. Maren is penciling notes in the margins of a printed requirements document from Corvane, her red pen moving methodically down the page as the light angles in. Julian is within earshot, hovering by the doorframe, and can't help overhearing a few key words. He glances at his watch, gauging if there's time before close of business to turn this into a tagline. Could Corvane's needs be his new slogan?

title: Watching the Run
prompt: Evening on the Open Floor. Owen announces the nightly full run in one flat word. The three of them turn to watch the first tests flicker onto Brody's latency graph. Theo picks at a snack from the shelf, trying to read the pattern. Brody taps the glass twice, then sits back, arms folded. Owen has his notebook open to the last clean page. Is tonight the night the run fails at 95% again?

title: The Merge Button
prompt: Evening on the Open Floor. Brody sits under his desk lamp, finger hovering over the merge button for today's last pull request. The day has been long and this change looks risky. Nora, sorting papers at the door to the Server Closet, glances over and wonders if she should step in. Brody taps the graph on his screen and frowns. Is it worth a late night if this fails?

title: Grey Box Vigil
prompt: Deep night in the Server Closet, lit only by Nora's flashlight. The door is propped open, as it has been before. Brody watches the grey box, tapping the latency graph against his palm. Nora keeps the beam steady on the green light, whispering 'easy' like a charm. Both listen for any change in the hum. What would they do if it stopped?

title: Release Review
prompt: Late evening in the Glass Box. Julian is sitting across from Graham's desk, reading out the draft release note with careful emphasis on each benefit. Graham, eyes on the ceiling, nods every other sentence, as if timing his agreement. The release is done; the notes are all that's left. Julian wants it perfect; Graham wants it signed. Is there really no change, or is one of them just tired?

title: Late Review
prompt: Deep night in the Glass Box. Graham is at his standing desk, laptop glow on his face, finishing a ticket comment with a few logistics metaphors. He signs off as 'GE' and glances at the dark street below. The office is silent, lights out, locked up for the night. He decides to hit send in the morning when the trains are running again. Should he log this as overtime?

title: Closing Tickets
prompt: Late evening in the Glass Box, the CEO's warm light spilling into the Open Floor. Graham sits at his desk, methodically reading out the day's open tickets and closing each one with a soft click of the mouse. Nearby, Brody lingers in the doorway, listening intently, ready to be drawn into discussion about any lingering issues. The room is heavy with the weight of a long day's work and the anticipation of its end. Will Graham's logistics metaphors bridge the gap between them, or will Brody's silence speak louder than words?

title: Late and Watched
prompt: Late at night on the Open Floor, Theo is the only one left working. The emergency light glows above the Party Member's silent corner desk. Theo, alone but for the silent watcher, keeps his screen turned away from the room. He tries to focus, but finds himself glancing over at the unmoving figure more and more often. Why does working late make everything feel different?

title: Odd Jar, Odd Hours
prompt: Late night in the dark Kitchen. Nora has let herself in to tidy up. She's puzzled by a jar with an unlabelled brown goo, so she labels it 'UNKNOWN' and dates it, then leaves a note on the door for the owner to claim it. The shelf it was on gets a quick reordering before she flicks off the light. Was it left there by accident or on purpose? And was this the last tidy thing, or the first untidy one?

title: Midnight Snack
prompt: Late night in the darkened Kitchen. Theo and Julian have each quietly made their way from their desks for a late-night snack from the shelf. Startled by the other's presence, they both try to play it cool, as if they were just about to head home anyway. Theo grabs a bag of chips while Julian reaches for a granola bar. The question hangs in the air: who will break the silence first and with what excuse for still being at the office at this hour?

title: Last in the Office
prompt: In the dark early hours, Graham stands in the doorway of the Glass Box, coat already on, one hand gripping the jamb. He's been here too late too often and wants to know what it will take to get the overnight build process unstuck. Brody is the last one left, at his desk with his coat on the back of his chair, not looking up from his screen. He gives Graham a short, technical answer that doesn't help. The rest of the office is empty and silent around them. Is there any point asking for more than Brody can or will say?

title: End-of-Day Oat Milk
prompt: It's late evening on the Open Floor. Maren is wrapping up her last task, focused on her neat points. Nora bustles over, a labelled oat milk carton in hand. 'Yours, I think,' she says brightly, setting it by Maren's keyboard. 'I'll keep the fridge tidy if you keep the floor in order!' Maren looks up, tired but grateful. Will she take the hint and head home soon? Or does she have one more point to make before she goes?

title: Night Thoughts
prompt: Deep night on the Open Floor, lit only by emergency lights and the glow from the Server Closet. Maren has come in to print a late report and pauses by the Party Member's desk, seeing the closed notebook and pen that have not moved since she started. For whom does he keep that silent vigil? What is the worth of the work she does? She gathers the dropped pages, straightens the printout, and goes back to her own desk without turning on the light.

title: Late Clearance
prompt: Late evening in the Kitchen. The Party Member's chair is empty, but their desk light is on. Nora, tidying up before she leaves, washes out the Party Member's unused cup from earlier and puts it away. She notices the Party Member's chair is in the exact same position as when she came in at 06:00. Did the Party Member even sit there today? Or is this just how they like it?

title: Puzzle Before Dawn
prompt: The Open Floor is dark and silent at 05:20. Maren sits alone at the window, the city still asleep behind her. A small pool of light from the desk lamp illuminates her crossword, which she fills in carefully with a fountain pen. The puzzle seems to demand her full concentration, but her mind keeps drifting to the day ahead and its responsibilities. How will she balance the needs of the clients and the team today?

title: Last One Out
prompt: Past midnight on the Open Floor, the lights are out and the room is dark. Owen, the Tester, sits at his desk in the gloom, the only light coming from his second monitor. He methodically coils the spare laptop's charger and drops it into a drawer. The test suite is running, its progress slow but inexorable. Owen's flat, deadpan expression doesn't change as he watches the numbers crawl. Is there anyone else still here, or is Owen the last one left in the office tonight?

title: Late Check

They all have good points, but only one version will make it out. Is clarity for everyone worth a longer list of codes?

title: For Whom?
prompt: Early morning on the Open Floor. Maren, pen tapping, stares at the red 'For whom?' she's just written at the top of a clean page, deciding how to structure today's plan. Julian, overhearing, wants to turn it into a smooth tagline but holds back, unsure if now is the right moment. He lingers nearby, leafing through customer images. Who is this work really for, and how will they know it?

title: Third Strike
prompt: Late afternoon on the Open Floor. Owen is at his desk with the spare laptop, watching a test fail for the third time. He writes a precise note about it. Anselm is nearby, within earshot, and could be drawn in. The room feels quiet, save for the soft hum of computers. Owen's pen hovers over the notebook, poised to write more. Will Anselm step in, or will Owen continue his methodical documentation alone?

title: Velocity and Analogies
prompt: Early morning in the Kitchen. Julian is restocking the snack shelf and asks Theo about the velocity rule in a recent update. Theo, halfway through a protein bar, launches into an explanation involving race cars and pit stops. Julian listens with a smile, but his eyes show he's not quite getting it. Theo senses this and starts to wonder if there's a better way to explain it. Can Theo find the right analogy to make the concept click for Julian?

title: Ostry Ticket
prompt: Morning on the Open Floor. Theo is grinning at a new Ostry ticket with an attention-grabbing title. He reads it aloud, enjoying the drama. Owen just asks for the ticket number. Theo's not sure if he's missing the point or making it. Is the ticket a false alarm or a real problem?

title: Biscuits and Banter
prompt: 06:45 in the Kitchen. Nora has the snack shelf open and is restocking from a small stack of boxes on the table, humming. Theo hovers nearby, reaching past her for the last of the cereal bars and two of the chocolate digestive biscuits. He's trying to draw her into conversation, but Nora is all business until the shelf is done and the boxes ticked off. She catches the second biscuit as it leaves the packet and holds it up. 'Really, Theo?' she asks, smiling. 'Two?'

title: Maren's Morning
prompt: Just before 09:00 on the Open Floor. Maren has finished the 06:00 standup and is sitting at her desk, carefully colouring the tab edges of a printout. He wonders what's first on her list and if it's something he should know about too. What will Maren say when she sees him listening?

title: Numbers and Noise
prompt: Late morning on the Open Floor. Brody is absorbed in a document, ignoring the chatter. Theo types steadily, making little satisfied noises. Owen announces a number, his first result of the day, and waits for it to sink in. Theo stops typing but doesn't turn around. Brody marks his place with a finger. What will it take for one of them to ask what the number means?
